description: Strictness backtest for the D4 relevance-gate rebalance (spec art_JBPvBRhF, deliverable D4).

corpora.docs/data.json promises: published records; before-gate state = recorded per-criterion scores; gold_set.json ids tagged gold_set_published
corpora.docs/data.json quarantined: 13 frozen rows incl. N12 (restated vote, real_promise 0) and P68 (non-SF, sf 0)
corpora.data/intake_candidate_register.json: 24 qualified candidates; gate booleans derived from frozen fields (statement_preview regexes, entity, promised_date, supervisor_district/geographic_scope)

style_classifier: capital_project = record_type project_or_opening or a street-address match in the text or address fields; else service_program

rebalance.same_artifact_cap: interesting contributes at most 1 when measurable is already 2 driven by the physical artifact (street address or filing/opening/count ID) and the text carries no distinct artifact of another class (dollar amount, filing ID, street address). Capping the number+date overlap was prototyped and rejected by this backtest: it cut quantified service programs while capital records escaped through their addresses, dollars, and IDs
rebalance.attribution_credit: interesting contributes 1 when raw interesting is 0, real_promise is 2 (verbatim quote + named speaker + date), and a named entity is present; because real_promise 2 forces measurable >= 1, this flips pass rates on sf_relevant-1 records and adds margin on sf_relevant-2 records
